notes: §1985:VI.5.12.3 SR1: "The SIGN clause may be specified only for a numeric data description entry whose PICTURE contains the character 'S', or a group item containing at least one such numeric data description entry." Run screens every data description entry that wrote a SIGN clause, in every section. An elementary entry goes to SignClauseElementaryDefect at every edition, which refuses one that is not of category numeric, has no S in its picture or has no PICTURE with COBOL2422. A group goes to GateGroupSignSubordinates, the 1985 arm (it returns at once from 2002): a group with no descendant that IsSignedNumericEntry accepts is refused through the construct sign-group-unsigned-subordinates-2002 with COBOL0900, which is the condition 2023 dropped. Probed at 85: SIGN on PIC X, PIC A, PIC -ZZ9, PIC 9(3), USAGE INDEX and on a group of alphanumeric and unsigned items is refused in the working-storage, file and linkage sections; SIGN on PIC S9 items at levels 01, 05 and 77 and on a group holding one signed item compiles. The witness is PIC 9(3) SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE, refused with COBOL2422.

next.reason: 1985 allows SIGN on a group only if the group contains 'at least one such numeric data description entry' (signed, PICTURE with S). 2023 §2023:13.18.52.3 SR1 allows it on 'an alphanumeric group item, national group item, or strongly-typed group item' with no such condition, and §2023:13.18.52.4 GR1 'applies only to numeric items whose picture character-string contains the symbol' S, so a group with no signed item is now accepted with no effect. Screen entries are new; report group entries were already allowed in the 1985 Report Writer module.
